suspend.title: Suspend {name}?
suspend.body: This takes {total, plural, one {the only branch} other {all # branches}} of {name} offline — {branches}. The storefront will return 404 — not the suspended screen. Staff keep their back-office access and no data is deleted. This does not change their subscription.

restore.title: Restore {name}?
restore.body: This brings back {total, plural, one {the only branch} other {all # branches}} of {name} — {branches}. Customers will be able to find the storefront again.
restore.bodyNoBranches: {name} has no branches, so there is nothing to bring back.
restore.warningUnpaid: {name}’s subscription is {status}, so the storefront will still show the suspended screen after restoring. Fix the subscription to bring them back online. <link>Manage subscription</link>
restore.warningPartial: {active} of {total} branches are already active. Restoring turns ALL {total} on, including any branch that was disabled deliberately.

reactivate.bodyExtendLive: Adds 1 month to the {plan} package the tenant already has{hasPrice, select, yes { at {price}/mo} other {}} for {seats, plural, one {# branch} other {# branches}}: paid through {from} becomes {to}. The store is still live, so diners notice nothing.
reactivate.bodyRebill: Re-bills the {plan} package the tenant already has{hasPrice, select, yes { at {price}/mo} other {}} for {seats, plural, one {# branch} other {# branches}}, paid through {to}. The storefront comes back on the diner’s next request.
reactivate.bodyConvert: Moves {name} off {current} and onto {plan}{hasPrice, select, yes { at {price}/mo} other {}} for {seats, plural, one {# branch} other {# branches}}, paid through {to}. The storefront comes back on the diner’s next request.
reactivate.warningSuspended: {suspended} of {total} branches are also platform-suspended and will keep returning 404 after this. Restore them separately.
